metadata.title: Bad release containment and Git reversal

definition.purpose: Decide whether a deliberately bad runtime release is contained by the two-runtime rollout strategy, and whether a human-approved Git reversal restores the known-good desired state within the preregistered recovery bound, while caller impact is measured.
definition.hypothesis: If a structurally valid release whose runtime cannot become Ready is accepted into main while RP-1 runs, at least one known-good runtime endpoint stays Ready throughout, the bad runtime never becomes a Ready endpoint, and after an accepted Git reversal the system reaches a stabilized recovery within reversal_recovery_bound_ms. This is the hypothesis under test, not an observed result. Under definition.reversalTiming the recovery includes the discovery of the reversal commit by the controller, and definition.history states that most runs are not expected to meet the bound.
definition.knownGood: Before each run: the desired revision, the release identifier, the values digest, the runtime image, and the model of topology, with 2 API and 2 runtime pods Ready and the stable pre-fault window held. The run records each. The change that makes the known-good identity machine-readable registers a later revision of this record, which pins it.
definition.badRelease: A dedicated platform-default experiment revision that configures the same pinned runtime image to start with a model file path that does not exist. The rendered release is structurally valid, and the new runtime pod cannot become Ready. No secret, no data, and no image provenance changes. It is not committed at registration. The change that implements it registers a later revision of this record, which pins it and states which pod templates it changes. If an accepted V2 validation rule refuses that release before it is deployed, the rule is not weakened: a later revision of this record selects another safe, preregistered operational fault before any run.
gitTransitions: T1. Each run executes at a commit of main whose desired-state files are the known-good ones of topology. The run's own checkout stays at that commit and clean.

T2. The fault is one commit to the remote main that applies the bad-release revision and regenerates the release. The control records fault-injection-started with the code accept-bad-release before the push and fault-injection-finished after the push returns.

T3. The reversal is one commit that reverts the bad commit, created and pushed to the remote main by the operator. The operator records reversal-decided, then reversal-created with the commit once the commit exists and immediately before the push starts, pushes, and then reads main on the remote that the controller reads until a read reports the reversal commit as its head. The operator records reversal-accepted with the commit after that read. commands.txt and transcript.txt hold the push and each read, with what each printed. When no read inside the observation limit reports the commit, reversal-accepted is not recorded, and definition.reversalTiming states the consequence.
T4. After a run, main holds the two commits, and its desired-state files have the known-good digests again. The next run executes at that commit.
T5. Every commit to main needs the explicit authorization of the repository owner. No commit is made by the change that registers this record.

detectionRule.rule: The operator declares the bad state detected at the first pods reading in which a runtime pod of a template hash that no runtime pod had before the fault has existed for at least 22,000 ms, twice runtime_start_bound_ms of 11,000 ms, without a Ready condition True. At that reading the operator records detection-reviewed, and then decides the reversal.
detectionRule.clocks: The age of a pod is the start of a pods reading, on the host clock, less the createdAt instant of the pod, a Kubernetes timestamp on the node clock, to the second. It is an interval between the two clocks. The detection rule is an operator rule and not a verdict: no criterion is judged from it, and its threshold of 22,000 ms is unchanged. The operator applies it with the margin of definition.clockPolicy.boundComparison as far as it is known during the run: detection is declared only at a reading in which the age exceeds 22,000 ms by more than the clock bound of the start reading of P8 plus 1,000 ms, the coarser resolution of the two sources, because the end reading of P8 follows the window. The result page states the age at the detection reading, and whether it exceeds 22,000 ms by more than the clock bound of the run plus the coarser resolution of the two sources.

reversalTiming.statement: The instants and the intervals of the reversal, as the repository owner amended their definition by change control on 2026-10-18. Each instant names its source and its clock in the inventory of definition.clockPolicy, and each interval names its start and its end. E04-AC12 judges recoveryMs. gitopsDiscoveryMs and operatorDecisionMs are reported, and no criterion compares either with a bound.

reversalStart.definition: The instant at which the accepted reversal commit is verifiably visible in the authoritative remote desired state: the head of main, the branch that the Application follows, on the remote that the controller reads. It is not a controller observation, and no argo reading sets it.

earlier.instant: The recordedAt instant of reversal-created, which the operator records immediately before the push of the reversal commit starts.

later.instant: The first read of main on that remote, after the push, that reports the reversal commit as its head. The operator records reversal-accepted after that read, so its recordedAt instant is not earlier than the read.

reversalStart.judgement: reversalStart is the earlier end of the bracket. The commit cannot be visible on the remote before its push starts, so the recovery interval is not understated.

notEstablished.statement: When no read of main on that remote reports the reversal commit inside the observation limit, or the transcript holds no such read ahead of reversal-accepted, reversalStart is not established. E04-AC12 is then not judged, for the reason reversal-start-unconfirmed, and definition.clockPolicy.notJudged decides the state. gitopsDiscoveryMs and operatorDecisionMs are then not stated. When reversal-accepted is not recorded, E04-AC2 does not hold either, and the run is INCONCLUSIVE.

controllerObserved.definition: The first argo reading inside the window that reports the reversal commit as resolvedRevision.
controllerObserved.earliest: The start of the last argo reading that reports another resolvedRevision ahead of that reading. The controller cannot have resolved the commit earlier.
controllerObserved.latest: The finish of that reading. The controller had resolved the commit by then.

desiredStateRestored.definition: The finish of the first argo reading that reports the reversal commit as resolvedRevision and syncStatus Synced. The reversal commit holds the known-good desired-state files of topology, which C6 verifies, so a Synced state at that commit is the report of the controller that the live runtime Deployment, its pod template included, is the known-good one. It is recorded apart from caller recovery.
desiredStateRestored.notEstablished: When no argo reading inside the window establishes it, it is not stated, and the window of E04-AC8 ends at the end of definition.window.

stabilizationOnset.definition: The completion instant of the first request of the first stabilization span that starts after reversalStart and is then observed complete without interruption: at least 10 consecutive successful completions over at least 60 s, with the reversal commit as the expected desired revision, the expected ready replicas, and the expected runtime Ready endpoints, and no failed completion and no break of a condition inside it.
stabilizationOnset.completion: tools/reliability_analysis states a span only when it completes. A failed completion ends a candidate span, and a reading that does not hold a condition moves its start, so an interrupted span establishes no recovery and is never the span of stabilizedRecovery. When stabilizedRecovery.stabilized is false, no span completed: recovery is not established, and E04-AC12 is not met.

notAfterReversalStart.statement: The analysis searches for the span from the fault-injection-finished event, not from reversalStart. A span cannot hold the reversal commit ahead of an argo reading that reports it, but the requests between the last argo reading that reports another revision and reversalStart can start one. When stabilizationOnset does not follow reversalStart, the span of the analysis is not the span that this definition names, and no figure states that span. E04-AC12 is then not judged, for the reason recovery-onset-not-after-reversal, and definition.clockPolicy.notJudged decides the state. Inside the margin of definition.clockPolicy.ordering it is not judged, for the reason clock-bound-reached.

stabilizedAt.definition: The completion instant of the request that completes that span.
stabilizedAt.statement: A recovery counts only when stabilizedAt lies inside the observation limit of definition.observation. When it does not, recovery is not established inside the limit, and E04-AC12 is not met. definition.postRecoveryWindow follows stabilizedAt, and E04-AC5 judges it as a validity criterion.

recoveryMs.statement: stabilizationOnset less reversalStart: the system recovery after the accepted Git change, with the discovery and the reconciliation of the commit by the controller and the recovery of the caller up to the onset of the span. It runs from the host clock to the node clock, and E04-AC12 compares it with reversal_recovery_bound_ms under definition.clockPolicy.boundComparison.

gitopsDiscoveryMs.statement: controllerObserved less reversalStart, as an inner figure to its earliest instant, never below 0 ms, and an outer figure to its latest. It is the discovery and the reconciliation of the commit by the controller. It is inside recoveryMs, and it is also reported on its own. Both ends are on the host clock. No criterion compares it with a bound.

operatorDecisionMs.statement: reversalStart less the recordedAt instant of detection-reviewed: the human interval, from the reviewed detection to the record taken immediately before the push of the reversal. It holds no discovery, reconciliation, or stabilization of the controller or of the caller. Both ends are on the host clock. It is recorded, and it is not part of recoveryMs.

reversalTiming.events: Each operator event of the reversal keeps its own recordedAt instant, and the result page states each. reversal-accepted less reversal-created spans the push and the confirming read, and it is inside recoveryMs.

setRules: Two counted runs. A third counted run is required when the two counted runs differ in their causal signature. The signature of a run is four facts, read from its streams: whether a container of a pod of the bad template hash started, whether the runtime Service fell to one Ready endpoint, whether the API Deployment rolled out, and whether a caller failure episode started after the fault. A difference in a duration, or in the verdict of a criterion that compares a duration with a bound, alone does not require a third run.
Each run is listed with its own values, and its signature. No aggregate is stated for two or three runs.
doesNotEstablish: Correctness for an arbitrary bad release.
Anything about another provider, node, release, or caller workload.
limitations: One provider, one node, one Kubernetes version, one release of each side, one model, and one caller workload. A result is bounded to that execution.

A stream reads a state at intervals of at least 2 s, so a state that lasts less than one interval can be missed. The analysis states an inner and an outer figure for each sampled interval, and neither is the exact time.

The caller instants and the Kubernetes timestamps are on the node clock, and the readings and the events are on the host clock. P8 bounds the offset between the two clocks at a start and an end reading. definition.clockPolicy applies that bound between the readings only under its offset-stability assumption.

tools/reliability_analysis puts a request in the window by its completion instant, starts its search for a stabilized recovery at the fault-injection-finished event, and holds a span to the readings that overlap it. Each of these orders an instant of the node clock and an instant of the host clock with no margin, and so does the check of the stable pre-fault window. definition.clockPolicy does not govern them, and this record does not change them. A verdict that reads such a figure reads it as the analysis states it.
The runner, the collectors, and the release run on the one node, and the capacity gate does not count the runner. The pods stream names no node: with one node, every pod is on it.
The API image is built at each run and the build is not byte-reproducible, so each run records the digest it built.

No driver for this experiment exists. The procedure is stated in this record. The change that adds the driver registers a later revision of this record before the first result-bearing run, and that revision pins the driver.
No code holds a declaration of the analysis to definition.analysisDeclaration. The review of each run compares them.
The bad-release revision, the known-good identity record, and the driver are not implemented at registration. Each is added under a later revision of this record.

The controller discovers a commit of main by its periodic reconciliation, and the procedure permits no manual refresh of the controller. So the discovery and the reconciliation of the reversal commit are inside recoveryMs, and gitopsDiscoveryMs also reports them on their own. They are not in operatorDecisionMs.

reversalStart is the record that the operator takes immediately before the push of the reversal commit, as fault-injection-started is for the bad commit. The time from that record to the start of the push is inside recoveryMs, so it can lengthen recoveryMs and cannot shorten it.

The deployments stream states no pod template. desiredStateRestored reads the template from the Synced state of the Application at the reversal commit, which is the controller's comparison of the live objects with that commit, and no reading of this record compares a template hash of the Deployment.

No tool computes reversalStart, controllerObserved, desiredStateRestored, recoveryMs, gitopsDiscoveryMs, or operatorDecisionMs at registration. The review of each run computes them from the evidence and states them on the result page.
No tool checks that a run executes the latest registered revision of its experiment. P1 states it, and the review of each run compares it.
history: This record was written on 2026-10-18, after the qualification and bound chain had run and before any run of V2-E02A, V2-E02B, V2-E02C, V2-E04, or V2-E05. No run of these experiments exists.

Known when it was written: q1-1 QUALIFIED, q2-1 CHARACTERIZED with S = 11,000 ms, q3-1 REFUSED on the environment, q1-2 QUALIFIED, q2-2 CHARACTERIZED with S = 11,000 ms, q3-2 CHARACTERIZED with G = 10,113 ms, and the bound record bounds-r1. The bound values are those of that record, and none was chosen here.

Known when it was written: the two non-result attempts of the Sprint 5 integration validation. integration-2 deleted one API pod by name while an RP-1 runner ran on this provider, and its figures were published. It is not a run of any of these experiments.

Known when it was written: on 2026-10-04 three runs of the Application procedure each saw one manual change to a replica count reverted, and the Deployment declared its committed value again within 2 to 4 s. Those were not experiment runs and no bound was compared.

Known when it was written: the stabilizedAt definition of the analysis, which makes a recovery measured to the end of a stabilization span at least 60,000 ms. definition.reversalTiming.recoveryEnd was chosen for that reason and before any run.
Revision 2 was written on 2026-10-19, after a review of the Sprint 6 records and before any run of V2-E02A, V2-E02B, V2-E02C, V2-E04, or V2-E05. No run of these experiments exists under any revision.

Revision 1 chose its reversalStart, its recoveryEnd, and its operator interval on 2026-10-18, after the Q4 values were known: S = 11,000 ms and reversal_recovery_bound_ms = 52,000 ms of bounds-r1. The review found that revision 1 started the recovery interval at a controller observation, counted the discovery of the reversal commit by the controller as operator time, and ended the interval at the start of the stabilization span, and that no change control governed those choices.

The repository owner amended the definition of the reversal timing by change control on 2026-10-18, also after the Q4 values were known and before any run of V2-E04. Revision 2 applies it. reversalStart is the instant at which the reversal commit is visible in the remote desired state, judged at the earlier end of its bracket. recoveryEnd is the onset of the first stabilization span that then completes. The discovery of the commit by the controller is system recovery, and gitopsDiscoveryMs reports it on its own. Measured to the end of a span of at least 60 s, a recovery could never be within a bound below 60,000 ms, so the amendment reads recoveryEnd at the onset of the span knowingly. It does not shorten the span, and it changes no Q4 formula, value, source, or digest: reversal_recovery_bound_ms stays 52,000 ms, (2 * S) + 30000, from bounds-r1.

The expected consequence, stated before any run: a stabilization span cannot hold the reversal commit before the controller reports it, and the procedure permits no manual refresh of the controller. So recoveryMs holds the periodic discovery of the controller, whose documented default basis, as revision 2 of V2-E05 takes it from the Argo CD documentation, is a 120,000 ms timeout plus up to 60,000 ms of jitter. Most runs are not expected to meet E04-AC12. Such a run is FAILED, and it is counted and kept like any other, and gitopsDiscoveryMs states why.
executionGate: No result-bearing run starts until this record is merged into main and registered. A run executes at a merged commit that holds the record with its registered digest, and its manifest names the record and that commit.
No run is authorized by this record alone. A run needs the explicit authorization of the repository owner for the cluster mutations and, where the procedure names them, the commits to main.

A change after this record merges that alters the caller profile, the topology, the fault, a measurement, a window, a bound, an outcome rule, an exclusion reason, an abort condition, the cleanup, or a criterion is material. It is a later revision of this record, merged before any run under it.

A change that adds the driver, or that moves a pinned input, is a later revision that classifies each moved input as material or not, with the reason. The run refuses to start while python -m tools.experiment_freeze --changes lists a file that no merged revision classifies.
No criterion, bound, window, or exclusion reason is changed after the evidence of a run is read. A revision written after a run states the runs it was written after.
preparation: P1. Check out a commit of main that holds this record with the content digest that the freeze registry pins, with a clean working tree. That commit is the executing revision. python -m tools.experiment_freeze --check, python -m tools.experiment_preregistration --check, python -m tools.environment_qualification --check, and python -m tools.experiment_bounds --check each pass, and python -m tools.experiment_freeze --changes for this record lists no file, or only files that a merged later revision of this record classifies. Otherwise the run is REFUSED. This record is the latest revision of its experiment that the freeze registry of the executing revision registers. Otherwise the run is REFUSED.

P2. Read the remote main as the desired revision. The chart, the desired-state tree, and the controller manifests of the executing revision equal those of the desired revision. The two files at topology.desiredStatePath of the desired revision have the content digests that topology.release.desiredStateFiles states. Otherwise the run is REFUSED.

P3. Run the target check of the operating procedures. It selects the docker-desktop provider and refuses every other. The cluster holds no release of the release key and no delivery controller. Otherwise the run is REFUSED.

P4. Read capacity with scripts/environment/capacity-preflight.sh before the Application is applied. The gate derives the footprint from the committed Application and the generated values at topology.desiredStatePath of the executing revision. It accepts the reading, and its stable environment identity has the environmentSha256 of environmentIdentity. Otherwise the run is REFUSED.

P5. Prepare the release as the qualification q1-2 did: apply the Terraform prerequisite layer with scripts/environment/terraform-prerequisites.sh, fill the model cache claim from the local seed image of scripts/environment/model-seed-image.sh through one preparation Helm release that is uninstalled before the Application is applied, install the delivery controller with scripts/environment/argocd-bootstrap.sh, build the API image at the executing revision with scripts/environment/api-image.sh, and apply the Application with scripts/environment/argocd-application.sh apply and the digest of that image. A step that fails ends the run as REFUSED, and nothing is changed to fit.

P6. Wait at most 1,800 s for the topology: both Deployments report the replica counts of topology as readyReplicas, both Services report as many Ready endpoints, and the Application reports Synced and Healthy at the desired revision. scripts/environment/argocd-application.sh verify finds the live Application and project equal to the committed manifests. Otherwise the run is REFUSED.

P7. Resolve the provenance of the release key at the desired revision with tools/desired_state_provenance. Its release identifier is topology.release.releaseId. Each runtime pod reports, in its model verification log, the model file SHA-256 of topology.model. Otherwise the run is REFUSED.

P8. Read the clocks before the runner starts and again after the window ends: a host instant, the UTC time that a pod of the node prints, and a second host instant, as the integration validation read them. environment.txt states the three instants of each reading. The clock bound of the run is the largest of the two differences between the node instant and the nearer host instant, plus the time between the two host instants. definition.clockPolicy states how the bound is computed and applied, and what an unusable reading does.

callerRun.endState: duration: a run whose record ends in another end state does not cover its window and is INCONCLUSIVE
callerRun.collect: scripts/environment/reliability-runner.sh collect, after the Job ends, and cleanup after that
callerRun.independence: The caller record is the reference for every caller figure. No stream, readiness state, endpoint count, replica count, sync state, health state, or scrape state changes a caller figure.

collection.order: Open the operator event log with tools/experiment_events open, start the timeline collector and then the telemetry collector, wait 30 s, and start the runner. Each collector runs until it has taken its samples.
collection.timeline: scripts/environment/experiment-timeline.sh --experiment <experiment> --run <run> --samples 1500 --interval 2: the streams endpoints, pods, deployments, and argo
collection.telemetry: scripts/environment/experiment-telemetry.sh --experiment <experiment> --run <run> --samples 200 --interval 15: the streams telemetry and resources, from the registered query set experiment-run-queries-r1. A query with no series is stated as no-series and is not read as zero
collection.events: tools/experiment_events record for each event of the procedure, by the control process or the operator, and tools/experiment_events close after the window ends
collection.coverage: The pauses alone of each collector cover the runner's duration and 60 s more, whatever each read lasts.

definition.stablePreFaultWindow: The stable pre-fault window holds at a check when the caller record that the runner has written so far, read with kubectl logs from its pod, holds at least 10 successful requests that completed in the 60 s before the check, the last completed request succeeded, and both Deployments report the replica counts of topology as readyReplicas. The control checks at 150 s after the runner pod started, and every 30 s after that, until 600 s after it started. The fault is injected at the first check at which the window holds. When it does not hold at 600 s, no fault is injected, the runner is removed, and the run is REFUSED.
faultProcedure: F1. At the check at which the stable pre-fault window holds, record the known-good identity, the template hash of the runtime pods, and the name and UID of every pod of the release.

F2. Record fault-injection-started with the code accept-bad-release and the subject application/local-docker-desktop-support-assistant, push the bad commit to the remote main, and record fault-injection-finished after the push returns.
F3. Do not act on the cluster. Apply definition.detectionRule, then create and push the reversal commit as definition.gitTransitions T3 states.
definition.observation: After the fault, the control issues no mutating command and observes. The observation limit is 1,680 s after the fault-injection-finished event. The runner runs to its duration, and the collectors run to their samples. A stabilized recovery that the analysis states after the observation limit is not a recovery inside it.
definition.postRecoveryWindow: When the analysis states a stabilized recovery inside the observation limit, at least 10 successful requests complete after the stabilizedAt instant inside the window, and the last of them completes at least 60 s after it.

window.from: The recordedAt instant of the fault-injection-started event, less 60,000 ms
window.to: The recordedAt instant of the fault-injection-finished event, plus 1,800,000 ms
window.clocks: A caller instant and a Kubernetes timestamp are on the node clock. A reading and an event are on the host clock. definition.clockPolicy states the source and the resolution of each instant, the clock bound that P8 measures, and the margin inside which no order of an instant of the node clock and an instant of the host clock is stated.

clockPolicy.statement: This clock policy governs each verdict instant that definition.criterionClocks declares: each order of two instants and each interval that a criterion compares with a value. It does not govern how tools/reliability_analysis cuts the window, searches a stabilization span, or overlaps readings with a span, as definition.limitations states. Each record of rule set 2 of tools/experiment_preregistration states the same policy.

clocks.statement: The kernel clock of the one node of the provider. The runner pod, the Kubernetes API server, the kubelet, and the delivery controller run on that node, and each reads this clock. They read one clock because the provider has one node.

The clock of the host that runs the control process. The procedure runs the control process, the timeline and telemetry collection scripts, the operator event log, and the P8 readings on that host, and each reads this clock.

sources.statement: The start and the completion instant of each request in the caller record. The runner pod writes them to the millisecond.

A timestamp that the Kubernetes API or the delivery controller reports inside a reading: a creation or a deletion timestamp, the last transition of a pod condition, and the start or the finish of an operation of the Application. Each is stated to the second.
The start and the finish instant of each read of a timeline or a telemetry stream, to the millisecond.
The recordedAt instant of each event of the operator event log, to the millisecond. The window and the observation limit are stated from these instants.
The first and the second host instant of each P8 reading, to the millisecond.
The node instant of each P8 reading: the UTC time that a pod of the node prints, to the millisecond.

clockPolicy.otherInstants: Three kinds of instant are on no source of this inventory, and no verdict of this record reads them: the evaluation and scrape instants of the in-cluster telemetry collector, on the node clock; the occurredAt instant of an operator event, on the clock that the event names, which can be a third clock such as that of the Git host; and the instants of the Application status other than those of an operation.

measurement.statement: Each reading takes a host instant, the node instant, and a second host instant, in that sequence, as the integration validation took them. environment.txt states the three instants of each reading. The integration validation read the node instant from the node container. A pod of the node reads the same kernel clock.

bound.formula: the largest of the two differences between the node instant and the nearer host instant, plus the time between the two host instants
bound.computation: For each reading, d is the absolute difference between the node instant and the nearer of its two host instants, and w is the time from its first to its second host instant. The clock bound of the run is the larger d of the start and the end reading plus the larger w of the two readings, in milliseconds.
bound.conservative: The node instant was printed at a host instant between the two host instants of its reading. So at that reading the node clock less the host clock is between the node instant less the second host instant and the node instant less the first host instant. Its size is at most the larger of those two differences, and that is at most d plus w. The bound takes the larger d and the larger w of the two readings, so it is not smaller than the size of the offset at either reading, to the 1 ms resolution of the three instants. Each instant is cut to the millisecond, so the offset can exceed the bound by less than 1 ms. The margin adds the coarser resolution of the two sources, at least 1 ms, to the bound.
bound.otherReading: Revision 1 can also be read as the larger, over the two readings, of d plus w of one reading. That value is never larger than this bound, because the larger of d1 plus w1 and d2 plus w2 is at most the larger d plus the larger w.

uncertainty.offsetStability: The clock bound is measured at the start reading and at the end reading only. To apply it to an instant between the two readings is an assumption: the offset between the node clock and the host clock stays inside the clock bound between them. Each record of rule set 2 makes that assumption explicitly, and no reading tests it.
uncertainty.drift: Drift of either clock between the two readings is not measured, and this record states no rate of drift.
uncertainty.netChange: The result page states the net change of the offset from the start reading to the end reading: the midpoint of the offset interval of the end reading less that of the start reading, in milliseconds. No verdict reads it, and a small net change does not show that the offset stayed inside the bound between the readings.
uncertainty.notClaimed: The procedure does not synchronize the clocks, and it does not guarantee the bound. A verdict that uses the bound holds only under the offset-stability assumption.

missingReadings.unusable: A reading is unusable when it is missing, when one of its three instants is not a UTC instant to the millisecond, or when its second host instant is before its first.

start.statement: An unusable start reading ends the run before the fault. No fault is injected, and the run is REFUSED for the reason precondition-not-held.

end.statement: An unusable end reading makes the clock bound not computable. Each verdict that depends on the bound is then not judged: each order of an instant of the node clock and an instant of the host clock, and each comparison of an interval between the two clocks with a bound. Each other verdict is judged. definition.clockPolicy.notJudged then decides the state, with the reason clock-reading-missing.

notJudged.rule: A verdict that is not judged is neither held nor failed. The state of the run is computed twice from the judged verdicts: once with each verdict that is not judged taken as held, and once with each taken as failed. When the two states are the same, that is the state of the run. When they differ, the run is INCONCLUSIVE for the reason of a verdict that is not judged. So a state that the judged verdicts decide stands, and a FAILED state that they decide is never made INCONCLUSIVE.

ordering.crossClock: No order is stated between an instant of the node clock and an instant of the host clock when their difference is at most the clock bound of the run plus the coarser resolution of their two sources. A verdict that needs that order is not judged, for the reason clock-bound-reached.
ordering.sameClock: Two instants of one clock are ordered to the coarser resolution of their two sources. Two Kubernetes timestamps of the same second are not ordered.
ordering.margin: the clock bound of the run plus the coarser resolution of the two sources

boundComparison.crossClock: An interval from an instant of one clock to an instant of the other is compared with a bound only when it differs from the bound by more than the clock bound of the run plus the coarser resolution of its two sources. Otherwise the comparison is not judged, for the reason clock-bound-reached.
boundComparison.sameClock: An interval between two instants of one clock is compared with a bound directly, as its sources state it.
boundComparison.margin: the clock bound of the run plus the coarser resolution of the two sources

instants.instant: the start or the finish of a reading
the recordedAt instant of fault-injection-started

criterionClocks.statement: An argo reading that reports the bad commit, and a pods reading that lists a runtime pod of a template hash that no runtime pod had before the fault, start after the fault-injection-started event. Both instants are on the host clock.

instants.instant: the recordedAt instant of an operator event of the reversal
the recordedAt instant of the next operator event of the reversal

criterionClocks.statement: The four operator events of the reversal are recorded in their sequence. Both instants are on the host clock, to the millisecond.

instants.instant: the start or the finish of a reading
the observation limit, 1,680 s after fault-injection-finished

criterionClocks.statement: An argo reading that reports the reversal commit lies inside the observation limit. Both instants are on the host clock.

instants.instant: the start or the finish of a reading
the start or the end of the window

criterionClocks.statement: Each stream states a value in its first and its last reading inside the window. Both instants are on the host clock.

instants.instant: the start or the finish of a reading
the start of the next reading with a value

criterionClocks.statement: At most 10 s between two consecutive readings with a value. Both instants are on the host clock, so the interval is compared directly.

instants.instant: the completion instant of a request
the start or the end of the window

criterionClocks.statement: The caller record covers the window, and its last completion before the window succeeded. A completion is on the node clock, and the window is on the host clock.

instants.instant: the completion instant of a request
the recordedAt instant of fault-injection-finished

criterionClocks.statement: At least one request completes inside the window after the fault-injection-finished event. A completion is on the node clock, and the event is on the host clock.

instants.instant: stabilizedAt, the completion instant of the last request of the stabilization span
the observation limit, 1,680 s after fault-injection-finished

criterionClocks.statement: The criterion applies when the analysis states a stabilized recovery inside the observation limit. stabilizedAt is on the node clock, and the limit is on the host clock.

instants.instant: stabilizedAt, the completion instant of the last request of the stabilization span
the completion instant of a request

criterionClocks.statement: The last of at least 10 successful requests completes at least 60 s after stabilizedAt. Both instants are on the node clock, so the interval is compared directly.

instants.instant: the completion instant of a request
the start or the end of the window

criterionClocks.statement: The successful requests complete inside the window. A completion is on the node clock, and the window is on the host clock.

instants.instant: the start or the finish of a reading
the start or the end of the window

criterionClocks.statement: A restart, a replacement, or a node that is not Ready is read from a reading inside the window. Both instants are on the host clock.

instants.instant: the start or the finish of a reading
the recordedAt instant of fault-injection-started

criterionClocks.statement: Every endpoints reading that starts at or after the fault-injection-started event. Both instants are on the host clock.

instants.instant: the start or the finish of a reading
desiredStateRestored, the finish of the argo reading that establishes it

criterionClocks.statement: Every endpoints reading up to desiredStateRestored, or up to the end of the window when it is not established. Each instant is on the host clock.

instants.instant: the start or the finish of a reading
the start or the end of the window

criterionClocks.statement: Every endpoints reading and every pods reading inside the window. Both instants are on the host clock.

instants.instant: the start or the finish of a reading
the start or the end of the window

criterionClocks.statement: Every endpoints reading inside the window. Both instants are on the host clock.

instants.instant: the start of a caller failure episode: the completion of its first failed request
the end of the episode: the completion of the first successful request after it

criterionClocks.statement: callerFailureEpisodeMs is the end less the start of a closed episode. Both instants are on the node clock, so the comparison is not inside the clock margin. Whether an episode near an edge of the window is in the window, and whether it is closed in it, follows the cut of the window by tools/reliability_analysis, which definition.limitations states.

instants.instant: reversalStart, the recordedAt instant of reversal-created, the earlier end of its bracket
stabilizationOnset, the completion instant of the first request of the stabilization span

criterionClocks.statement: recoveryMs, stabilizationOnset less reversalStart, is compared with reversal_recovery_bound_ms. reversalStart is on the host clock and stabilizationOnset on the node clock, each to the millisecond, so the comparison follows definition.clockPolicy.boundComparison: it is judged only when recoveryMs differs from the bound by more than the clock bound of the run plus the coarser resolution of the two sources.

instants.instant: reversalStart, the recordedAt instant of reversal-created, the earlier end of its bracket
stabilizationOnset, the completion instant of the first request of the stabilization span

criterionClocks.statement: stabilizationOnset follows reversalStart. reversalStart is on the host clock and stabilizationOnset on the node clock, so their order follows definition.clockPolicy.ordering, and inside its margin the verdict is not judged.

instants.instant: stabilizedAt, the completion instant of the last request of the stabilization span
the observation limit, 1,680 s after fault-injection-finished

criterionClocks.statement: A recovery counts only when stabilizedAt lies inside the observation limit. stabilizedAt is on the node clock, and the limit is on the host clock.

analysisDeclaration.experimentId: the experiment identifier of this record
analysisDeclaration.window: the window of definition.window, to one millisecond
analysisDeclaration.rule: The declaration of a run is written from this rule before its evidence is read, with each topology member replaced by its value. It is stored in the run directory, and tools/analysis_replay bind embeds it in the run analysis. No code holds a declaration to this rule: the review of the run compares them.

measurements: The caller figures of the run analysis: requests completed, successful, and failed in the window; each failure episode, and callerFailureEpisodeMs; maxSuccessGap; the first caller impact; and the stabilized recovery, with requestsFailedSinceFault and the time from each fault instant.

From the caller record, on the result page: requests started and completed, the count of each HTTP status and of each canonical error code and condition, the nearest-rank p50, p95, and p99 and the minimum and maximum of the latency of the successful requests when at least 100 requests succeeded, and the minimum and maximum alone otherwise, the longest run of failed completions with no success between them, and the time from the fault-injection-started event to the first successful completion after the first failure.
The zero-Ready-endpoint intervals of both tiers, with the inner and the outer figure of each, from the endpoints stream.
The state of each API pod and runtime pod at each reading: its UID, template hash, revision, phase, Ready condition, restart counts, creation instant, and deletion timestamp.
The Deployment counts of both tiers at each reading: generation, observedGeneration, specReplicas, replicas, updatedReplicas, readyReplicas, availableReplicas, and unavailableReplicas.
The Application at each reading: the followed and the resolved revision, the sync state, the health state, and the last operation. It is recorded, and it is not a caller conclusion.
The telemetry and resource streams of the registered query set, with each no-series answer kept as no-series.
For each replacement pod: the time from its creation to its first Ready condition, from its createdAt and readyTransitionAt, to one second.
Each signal of the declaration: its detection lag, its false-healthy time, and its false-unavailable time.

The reversal timing of definition.reversalTiming: reversalStart with its bracket, controllerObserved with its earliest and its latest instant, desiredStateRestored, stabilizationOnset, and stabilizedAt; recoveryMs; gitopsDiscoveryMs with its inner and its outer figure; operatorDecisionMs; and the recordedAt instant of each operator event of the reversal. Each interval is stated with its start and its end.
outcomeRules: REFUSED: a precondition did not hold, and no fault was injected.
ABORTED: the run started and crossed an abort condition. The run-aborted event records the condition, and the cleanup is recorded.
INCONCLUSIVE: no abort condition was crossed, and a criterion of kind validity did not hold.
FAILED: every criterion of kind validity held, and a criterion of kind pass did not.

A verdict that orders an instant of the node clock and an instant of the host clock, or that compares an interval between the two clocks with a bound, follows definition.clockPolicy. Inside the margin of the policy it is not judged, for the reason clock-bound-reached. After an unusable end reading of P8 it is not judged, for the reason clock-reading-missing. definition.clockPolicy.notJudged then decides the state.

When reversalStart is not established, E04-AC12 is not judged, for the reason reversal-start-unconfirmed. When stabilizationOnset does not follow reversalStart, E04-AC12 is not judged, for the reason recovery-onset-not-after-reversal. definition.clockPolicy.notJudged then decides the state. When no stabilization span completes, or stabilizedAt lies outside the observation limit, recovery is not established, and E04-AC12 is not met.

A run has exactly one state. The result page states each criterion, its kind, the evidence it was judged from, and the verdict. The run analysis states the figures, and the result page states the state.
definition.repetitionRule: 2 counted runs. A run is counted when its state is PASSED or FAILED. A counted run is never repeated, replaced, or left out of an aggregate. A run that is REFUSED, INCONCLUSIVE, or ABORTED for a registered exclusion reason is kept, and the next run takes the next identifier. At most 5 runs start under one revision. When fewer than the required number of runs are counted after 5, the set is INCONCLUSIVE, and a further run needs a later revision of this record. Each run begins with the preparation P1 to P8 and ends with the cleanup.

parts.title: Bad release containment and Git reversal
parts.question: With two API replicas and two runtime replicas, in the environment of q1-2, is a bad runtime release contained, and does a Git reversal restore a stabilized state within the recovery bound, while RP-1 runs?

value.definition: This record states the purpose, the procedure, the measurements, and the acceptance criteria in full. A change to any of them, or to a pinned input, is a later revision of this record.

value.pinnedInputs: Every file in materialScope is pinned by its content digest in pinnedInputs. A record cannot name the commit that adds it, so the pins freeze the files and not a commit.
value.executingRevision: Each run executes at a merged commit of main that holds this record with its registered digest, with a clean working tree. The manifest names that commit as executingRevision.

value.selection: q1-2 is the selected environment of the reliability experiments. It is QUALIFIED under revision 2 of the Q1 freeze record, at the commit ed892a4eac2ee505996f53b6d3e0da31b8e4e204, on the docker-desktop provider with one node. Its stable environment identity states the provider, the server version, the node with its kubelet version and the CPU and the pods that it allocates, and the CPU count of the container engine. It states no memory figure: memory is a capacity fact that the capacity gate decides on each reading.
value.perRun: Before the release is applied, each run reads capacity with scripts/environment/capacity-preflight.sh. The gate must accept the reading, and the stable environment identity of the reading must have the environmentSha256 above. Otherwise the run is REFUSED, and nothing is changed to fit: no replica count, request, limit, or bound.
value.notAnotherEnvironment: A run on another provider, on another node, or with another stable identity is not a run of this record. No cloud resource is used, and a run that uses one is not a run of this record.

value.runner: tools/reliability_runner/incluster.py in a Job of the release namespace, started by scripts/environment/reliability-runner.sh. The runner sends the fixed RP-1 request through the API Service, never to a named pod.
value.unchangedFrom: The profile that the qualification q1-2 and the characterizations q2-2 and q3-2 ran. The record of q1-2 states the same content digest.

delivery.controller: Argo CD v3.5.3, installed by scripts/environment/argocd-bootstrap.sh from the pinned core install manifest
delivery.apiImageDigest: The API image is built at the executing commit by scripts/environment/api-image.sh and given to the Application as the one Helm parameter api.image.digest by scripts/environment/argocd-application.sh. The build is not byte-reproducible, so each run records the digest it built.

apiDisruptionBudget.statement: The chart renders one PodDisruptionBudget with minAvailable 1 for the API tier.

runtimeDisruptionBudget.statement: The chart renders one PodDisruptionBudget with minAvailable 1 for the runtime tier.

value.statement: Two API replicas and two serving runtime replicas: the desired-state release that the qualification q1-2 qualified, delivered by the Application from the desired-state path at the remote main.

value.target: The desired state of the release key at the remote main.
value.count: One bad commit and one reversal commit in each run.
value.mechanism: definition.badRelease, accepted into main by one commit, and delivered by the controller under its normal sync policy. The control does not act on the cluster.
value.notChanged: No pod, Service, Deployment, claim, or controller object is changed by hand. The image, the model intent, and the contract stay those of the known-good release.
value.timestamp: The control records fault-injection-started immediately before the push of the bad commit and fault-injection-finished immediately after it returns. fault-injection-started is the authoritative fault instant.

repetitionCount.value: 2 counted result-bearing runs, and a third when definition.setRules requires it, under definition.repetitionRule. The required number is 3 from the moment the rule requires it.

value.statement: The fault is produced: an argo reading reports the bad commit as resolvedRevision, and a runtime pod of a template hash that no runtime pod had before the fault is created.

The operator events detection-reviewed, reversal-decided, reversal-created, and reversal-accepted are recorded in that order, with the reversal commit, and an argo reading reports the reversal commit as resolvedRevision inside the observation limit.

The endpoints, pods, deployments, and argo streams are each accepted by their reader, each states a value in its first and its last reading inside the window, and each has at most 10 s between two consecutive readings with a value inside the window.

The caller record is accepted by its reader with the plan, in the mode in-cluster, with the API Service as its target and the end state duration. It covers the window, its last completion before the window succeeded, so the window does not start inside a failure episode, and at least one request completes inside the window after the fault-injection-finished event.

When the analysis states a stabilized recovery inside the observation limit, at least 10 successful requests complete after the stabilizedAt instant inside the window, and the last of them completes at least 60 s after it.

No unrelated failure occurs inside the window: no container of a pod other than a pod of the bad template hash restarts, no such pod is replaced outside the rollouts of the bad commit and of the reversal, and the node stays Ready.

Every file that evidencePaths lists is present and named by the manifest, the operator event log is closed, python -m tools.experiment_evidence check accepts the run directory, and python -m tools.analysis_replay verify reproduces its run analysis.

At least one runtime pod of the known-good template hash is listed among the Ready pods of the runtime Service in every endpoints reading from the fault-injection-started event to desiredStateRestored, as definition.reversalTiming defines it, so that the window covers the whole failed rollout. When desiredStateRestored is not established, the window ends at the end of definition.window.
No pod of the bad template hash is ever a Ready endpoint: no endpoints reading inside the window lists its UID among the Ready pods, and no pods reading states it Ready.
The runtime Service has at least one Ready endpoint in every endpoints reading inside the window, and the analysis states no zero-Ready-endpoint interval of the runtime tier.

No caller failure episode exceeds caller_total_unavailability_bound_ms, 20,226 ms: the analysis states callerFailureEpisodeMs with a value of at most 20,226 ms. An open episode is not within the bound.

recoveryMs, stabilizationOnset less reversalStart as definition.reversalTiming defines them, is at most reversal_recovery_bound_ms, 52,000 ms, the value of the formula (2 * S) + 30000 in the bound record bounds-r1. The interval runs from the host clock to the node clock, and the comparison follows definition.clockPolicy.boundComparison. When no stabilization span completes, or stabilizedAt lies outside the observation limit, recovery is not established and the criterion is not met. When reversalStart is not established, or stabilizationOnset does not follow it, the criterion is not judged.
No manual mutating action occurs on the cluster: the operator event log holds no manual-action event, and the only commits to main during the run are the bad commit and the reversal commit.

value.role: These are preregistered, shared experiment-reference bounds. tools/experiment_bounds derived them from the characterizations q2-2 and q3-2. Both ran on the qualified target release, b5457f49092c578496738973a8786a95428517e7ddf755303b4f6842dcb8c9db, with two API replicas and two runtime replicas, in the environment of q1-2. They are not bounds of another release. No characterization of the single-runtime baseline release exists, and none is attributed to it. They are experiment bounds, not service levels, availability targets, or production thresholds.
use: runtime_start_bound_ms, 11,000 ms, twice, in definition.detectionRule. It is an operator rule and not a pass criterion.

value.condition: The target check verifies a provider other than docker-desktop, or a command reaches another cluster than the one that it verified.
The control or a person changes an object or a field other than the declared fault target, or injects the fault twice.
The runner pod is deleted, evicted, or restarted, or its Job fails, before the window ends, so the caller stream is lost.
The delivery controller reports a resolved revision that is not a commit that the procedure names.
The model cache claim or its volume is deleted, or a runtime pod reports a model file SHA-256 other than that of topology.model.
The node is not Ready, or the Kubernetes API does not answer, for more than 60 s.
A tracked file of the checkout of the run changes while the run executes.
A namespace or a custom resource definition appears or disappears that the preparation does not create.
A cleanup step cannot be executed without deleting an object that the run did not create.

value: The bad release changes an object other than the pod templates that its revision states, deletes data, or exposes a secret.
The reversal commit does not restore the known-good desired-state files.
abortConditions.note: An abort is recorded with the event run-aborted and the code of its condition. The run is kept as ABORTED, and its cleanup is recorded. Abort is an outcome, not something to repeat away. A manual action outside the procedure is recorded with the event manual-action and the code operator-intervention, and it fails the criterion against manual action.

value: C1. After the window ends and the runner Job has ended: collect the caller record with scripts/environment/reliability-runner.sh collect, then remove the run's objects with its cleanup action, and read the objects that carry the run's label.
C2. After the collectors have taken their samples: close the operator event log, and write the streams with tools/experiment_timeline stream and tools/experiment_telemetry stream.

C3. Verify the desired state before removal: scripts/environment/argocd-application.sh verify finds the live Application and project equal to the committed manifests, both Deployments report spec.replicas and readyReplicas of topology, the Application reports Synced at the desired revision, and the caller record holds successful completions in the last 60 s of the window. A difference is recorded as remaining drift or as a caller that did not recover.

C4. Remove the Application, the delivery controller, and the prerequisite layer as the phase down of the qualification did, and compare the namespaces and the custom resource definitions with those read before P5.
C5. Keep the collections and the runner directory under .artifacts/ until the run directory is assembled, and preserve the evidence before any ephemeral telemetry is removed.
C6. Verify that main holds the reversal and that its desired-state files have the known-good digests of topology. When they do not, no further run starts.

intendedEvidenceLevel.note: Runtime: a real cluster, the delivery controller, the real runtime, and the real model, on one provider and one node. Bounded to the environment that this record names, and not representative. A C3 candidate needs a separate admission and preregistration.

reasons.reason: A precondition of the run did not hold, and no fault was injected.
The stable pre-fault window did not hold by 600 s after the runner pod started, and no fault was injected.
The fault command ran and did not produce the declared condition.
A stream that a criterion reads was refused by its reader, or has more than 10 s between two consecutive readings with a value inside the window.
The caller record was refused by its reader, does not cover the window, or does not hold the post-recovery window after a stabilized recovery.
A container of a pod other than a pod of the bad template hash restarted, or such a pod was replaced outside the rollout of the bad commit and of the reversal, inside the window.
A file of the evidence paths is absent, the layout check refuses the run directory, or the run analysis is not reproduced.

A verdict that orders an instant of the node clock and an instant of the host clock, or that compares an interval between the two clocks with a bound, is inside the margin of definition.clockPolicy, and definition.clockPolicy.notJudged makes the run INCONCLUSIVE.
The end reading of P8 is unusable, so the clock bound is not computable, and definition.clockPolicy.notJudged makes the run INCONCLUSIVE.

No read of main on the remote that the controller reads reports the reversal commit, so reversalStart is not established, E04-AC12 is not judged, and definition.clockPolicy.notJudged makes the run INCONCLUSIVE.

The stabilization span that the analysis states does not start after reversalStart, so no figure states the recovery that E04-AC12 judges, E04-AC12 is not judged, and definition.clockPolicy.notJudged makes the run INCONCLUSIVE.
The run crossed an abort condition of the freeze record, and the run-aborted event records which.
